alternates.ref: Complete Works, Vol. 8, Epistles – Fourth Series, XXIII, p. 316
alternates.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
alternates.setting: Letter to the Hale sisters, autumn 1894: even he admits his faith wavers.
alternates.line: What a rogue am I that in the face of such mercies sometimes the faith totters — seeing every moment that I am in His hands.
alternates.translation: Glory unto Jagadambâ (Mother of the Universe)! I have gained beyond expectations. The prophet has been honoured and with a vengeance. I am weeping like a child at His mercy — He never leaves His servant, sisters. The letter I send you will explain all, and the printed things are coming to the American people. The names there are the very flower of our country. The President was the chief nobleman of Calcutta, and the other man Mahesh Chandra Nyâyaratna is the principal of the Sanskrit College and the chief Brahmin in all India and recognised by the Government as such. The letter will tell you all. O sisters! What a rogue am I that in the face of such mercies sometimes the faith totters — seeing every moment that I am in His hands. Still the mind sometimes gets despondent. Sister, there is a God — a Father — a Mother who never leaves His Children, never, never, never. Put uncanny theories aside and becoming children take refuge in Him. I cannot write more — I am weeping like a woman.

verse.speaker: Rama
verse.setting: After the war, Lakshmana finds Rama alone and asks how to cross the sea of confusion.
verse.sanskrit: यदन्यदन्यत्र विभाव्यते भ्रमादध्यासमित्याहुरमुं विपश्चितः । असर्पभूतेऽहिविभावनं यथा रज्ज्वादिके तद्वदपीश्वरे जगत् ॥
verse.line: Confusion sees one thing as another, a rope as a snake. Look again.
verse.translation: The wise call it superimposition when, through confusion, one thing is taken for another, as a snake is seen in a rope; so the world is seen in the Lord.
verse.why: Much of our fear is a rope mistaken for a snake; look again.

prasang.title: The rope and the snake
prasang.summary: Rama explains that the Self is never born and never dies, that suffering comes from mistaking one thing for another like a rope for a snake, and that in deep sleep, free of wanting, we simply feel happy.
prasang.lesson: Much of our fear is a rope mistaken for a snake; look again.

why: names the mechanism of misperception
Teach me simply how to cross over.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna admits the confusion of the world is hard to get through, and says who gets through it.
verse.sanskrit: दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया । मामेव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायामेतां तरन्ति ते ॥
verse.line: This tangle is hard to get through. Those who take shelter in me get through it.
verse.translation: This divine power of mine, made of the three qualities, is very hard to get past. Those who take refuge in me alone cross beyond it.
verse.for_you: Yesterday confusion was named. Today a path is offered through the hard tangle of the world. You do not need to see clearly to find your way forward today.

why: the confusion is named as truly hard to get through, and a way through is given
effort alone was never expected to be enough

verse.speaker: Vidura
verse.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verse.sanskrit: न देवा यष्टिमादाय रक्षन्ति पशुपालवत् / यं तु रक्षितुमिच्छन्ति बुद्ध्या संयोजयन्ति तम्
verse.line: The gods don't stand guard with a stick; whom they protect, they give clear judgement.
verse.translation: The gods do not guard a person with a stick in hand, the way a herdsman guards cattle. Whomever they wish to protect, they endow with good judgement.
verse.why: Character shows under pressure. Do by day what will let you sleep at night.

prasang.title: Vidura Niti: Keshini's choice and the tests of character
prasang.summary: Vidura tells how Prahlada judged honestly against his own son when Princess Keshini set two suitors a test, then gives aphorisms: gold is tested by fire, friends by hard times, and a clear conscience lets you sleep.
prasang.lesson: Character shows under pressure. Do by day what will let you sleep at night.

verse.try_today: Notice one small moment of clear judgement in your day, however brief.
verse.scene_line: You stand in the quiet of your home, and Vidura speaks to you of a king who cannot sleep.

why: Answers 'why does no one protect me' by pointing to the judgement one has been given
Help arrives as clarity

verse.line: Lead us by the good path. Keep crooked dealing far from us.
verse.translation: O Agni, lead us by the good path to true wealth, O god who knows all our ways. Keep crooked wrongdoing away from us. We offer you our fullest words of reverence.
verse.why: Hold what you have lightly, keep working, and see yourself in everyone.

prasang.title: The Isha: enjoy by letting go

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna's final counsel: act with devotion, reflect, choose, and take refuge.
verse.sanskrit: इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया । विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥
verse.line: I've told you all I know. Reflect on it fully, then do as you choose.
verse.translation: Thus I have declared to you this knowledge, more secret than all secrets. Reflect on it fully, and then do as you wish.
verse.why: Reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear.

prasang.title: Action with devotion: surrender
prasang.summary: Krishna urges Arjuna to offer all action, warns that ego will only trip him, tells him to reflect fully and then choose, and finally to take refuge in him alone and not grieve.
prasang.lesson: Reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear.

verse.for_you: Yesterday you asked to be led on a good path. Today you are asked to reflect fully on what you have heard and then choose your own way forward. That choice begins with the teaching you have just received.
verse.try_today: Pause before your next decision. Reflect on what you have heard. Then choose what you will do.
verse.scene_line: You stand at a crossroads with many paths before you, and you are asked to weigh them carefully before you step.

why: full reflection before acting is the instruction
Reflect fully, then decide and begin.

story.title: Karunya stops acting: knowledge and action as two wings
story.story_hook: Karunya came home from his studies so full of questions that he stopped doing anything at all.
story.summary: A student asks the sage Agastya whether freedom comes from action or from knowledge. Agastya answers with a story: young Karunya, confused by two scriptures, simply stopped doing anything, and his father had to show him that understanding and action work together.
story.lesson: Don't freeze while you wait to be sure. Understanding and action have to fly together.
story.hook_title: A bright student got so confused by everything he had studied that he stopped doing anything
story.teaser: A bright student got so confused by everything he had studied that he stopped doing anything

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna, who asks why he must act at all if understanding is higher.
verse.sanskrit: व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे । तदेकं वद निश्चित्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम् ॥
verse.line: Your advice sounds mixed and confuses me. Tell me the one thing I should do.
verse.translation: With these seemingly mixed words you confuse my mind. Tell me decisively that one thing by which I may reach the highest good.
verse.why: Not acting is still a choice; do the work that is yours.

prasang.title: Why doing your duty without attachment is better
prasang.summary: Arjuna is confused and asks for one clear answer. Krishna says no one can stop acting, that repressing the body while the mind indulges is self-deception, and that action beats inaction.
prasang.lesson: Not acting is still a choice; do the work that is yours.

verse.for_you: You are asking for one clear thing after losing your father. You feel caught between thinking your way through this and acting your way through it. The highest good is found in doing what is in front of you right now.
verse.try_today: Do only what is right in front of you today.

why: 'you are confusing my understanding'
Your advice sounds contradictory. Should I think my way out or act my way out?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on those who miss him and those who know him.
verse.sanskrit: इच्छाद्वेषसमुत्थेन द्वन्द्वमोहेन भारत । सर्वभूतानि संमोहं सर्गे यान्ति परन्तप ॥
verse.line: From the pull of want and push of dislike comes the confusion that traps every being.
verse.translation: Through the delusion of the pairs of opposites, arising from desire and aversion, Bharata, all beings fall into confusion at birth, scorcher of enemies.
verse.why: Pull and push of like and dislike are what confuse us.

prasang.title: Those who miss the Lord and those who know him
prasang.summary: The deluded see only the outer form; desire and aversion confuse all beings. Those freed from confusion come to know the divine fully.
prasang.lesson: Pull and push of like and dislike are what confuse us.

verse.for_you: Today the Gita says this confusion comes from wanting and not wanting. You are caught between wanting your father back and not wanting this grief.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment of wanting or disliking today.
verse.scene_line: Krishna names the pairs of opposites that trap every being, including you as you stand between wanting and not wanting.

why: The confusion of opposites (Bhagavad Gita 7.27)
confusion is the common starting condition, produced by liking and disliking

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला । समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि ॥
verse.line: Pulled by conflicting advice, the mind wobbles. When it settles and stays still, you've arrived.
verse.translation: When your understanding, now confused by conflicting things you have heard, stands firm and unmoving in deep stillness, then you will attain yoga.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.for_you: Yesterday said confusion comes from wanting and not wanting. Today, the mind wobbles from too many voices. When your understanding stands firm and still, you arrive.
verse.try_today: Notice when your understanding stands still and unmoving.
verse.scene_line: You stand at the crossroads of too many voices, as Krishna steadies Arjuna.

why: confusion from conflicting voices is expected, and it can settle
the wobbling ends when the understanding settles in stillness

verse.speaker: Garuda
verse.setting: Garuda, his doubt resolved, thanks Kakbhushundi.
verse.sanskrit: जो अति आतप ब्याकुल होई। तरु छाया सुख जानइ सोई॥ जौं नहिं होत मोह अति मोही। मिलतेउँ तात कवन बिधि तोही ॥
verse.line: Only the one scorched by the sun knows the shade. Without my doubt, I'd never have found you.
verse.translation: Only one scorched by the sun knows the comfort of a tree's shade. Friend, had I not been so deeply confused, how would I ever have met you?
verse.why: Doubt is human; stay long enough in good company and it can lead somewhere better.

prasang.title: Garuda's doubt
prasang.summary: Garuda, Vishnu's own mount, frees Ram from a serpent-noose in battle and starts to doubt: how can God be bound? He goes to Narada, Brahma and Shiva, who sends him to an old crow, Kakbhushundi, saying doubts clear only with long time in good company. Kakbhushundi tells him no one has escaped delusion, desire, craving or anger; Garuda ends up grateful for the doubt that led him there.
prasang.story_hook: The great eagle Garuda flew to a crow to ask a question.
prasang.lesson: Doubt is human; stay long enough in good company and it can lead somewhere better.

verse.for_you: Yesterday, Krishna said the mind wobbles. Today, the sun taught Garuda that shade is only known to those who have burned. You do not need to fix your grief. You only need to let the heat teach you where to rest.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment today when your heat is so great that it points you toward a place of rest.
verse.scene_line: Like Garuda, you stand in the heat of your questions, and the shade of this verse meets you there.

verse.speaker: Parvati
verse.setting: Parvati answers the sages who mock her resolve to win Shiva through years of austerity.
verse.sanskrit: सत्य कहेहु गिरिभव तनु एहा। हठ न छूट छूटै बरु देहा॥ कनकउ पुनि पषान तें होई। जारेहुँ सहजु न परिहर सोई ॥
verse.line: Gold comes from stone, and even in fire it stays gold. Hold to what you are.
verse.translation: You speak truly: this body was born of a mountain, so its resolve will not break, even if the body does. Gold too is born of stone, and even in fire it does not give up its nature.
verse.why: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.
verse.misuse: Steadiness is not stubbornness; keep checking that the goal is still worth it.

prasang.title: Parvati holds to her choice
prasang.summary: Reborn as Parvati, Sati resolves to marry Shiva and spends years in austerity. The seven sages come to test her, mocking Shiva as a homeless ascetic and offering her a better match. She answers that gold keeps its nature even in fire, and that the heart wants the one it has chosen.
prasang.story_hook: The sages came to talk Parvati out of it, and they listed every flaw in the man she had chosen.
prasang.lesson: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.

verse.for_you: Now Parvati speaks: your resolve will not break even if the body does. Hold to what you are.
verse.try_today: Notice one thing today that stays the same even when it changes.

why: a resolve that does not bargain when tested

story.title: Uddalaka's lessons: tat tvam asi
story.summary: Uddalaka teaches his son through everyday experiments: a fast that dims the mind, a bird on a string, rivers merging in the sea, a banyan seed with nothing visible inside, salt dissolved in water, a blindfolded man finding his way home. Each lesson ends: 'That subtle essence is the self of all. You are that, Shvetaketu.'
story.lesson: What is most real in you is unseen, everywhere, and the same in all.
story.for_you: Hold to your resolve, and then take the next step. You do not have to see the whole path. One true direction plus your own steps gets you home.

plan_v3.path: st.up.man_from_gandhara -enacts_in-> bhaya, moha ; st.up.man_from_gandhara -enacts_turn-> sankalpa, shraddha, viveka
why: Lost is not the same as hopeless; one true direction plus your own steps gets you home.

queries.hook: The wish to understand what these texts teach, and to find in them something steady to lean on.
queries.diagnose: Loneliness and emptiness come from feeling separate from people, purpose and the divine; the heart is searching for where it belongs.
queries.steady: You belong more than you feel right now; the people and the practice that hold you are still within reach.
queries.act: Reach out to the people and the practice that hold you; seek good company, and remember you are never truly alone.
queries.story: A story of a student who came to a teacher with questions and was led, step by step, toward the truth.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.setting: From 'Weighing the Lasting and the Passing': not knowing how to spend a short life.
verse.sanskrit: तपस्यन्तः सन्तः किमधिनिवसामः सुरनदीं गुणोदारान्दारानुत परिचरामः सविनयम् । पिबामः शास्त्रौघानुत विविधकाव्यामृतरसान् न विद्मः किं कुर्मः कतिपयनिमेषायुषि जने ॥
verse.line: Retreat, family, study or art? We cannot choose, and a life lasts only a few blinks.
verse.translation: Shall we live as ascetics beside the heavenly river? Or courteously serve our wives, generous in virtue? Or drink the floods of scripture, or the nectar of many kinds of poetry? We do not know what to do, in a human life that lasts a few blinks.
verse.why: Do what matters most while you still can.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Weighing the lasting and the passing
prasang.summary: Weighing what lasts: religion without inner peace is trading; old age can bring neglect; act while healthy, not when the house is on fire. The poet admits not knowing how to spend a short life.
prasang.lesson: Do what matters most while you still can.

verse.for_you: You are standing at a crossroads after a great loss, asking what comes next. The poem admits it does not know which path is right, only that the time is short.
verse.try_today: Notice one small thing that brings you quiet presence today.
verse.scene_line: You stand at the edge of many good paths, unsure which one to take.

why: Unable to choose among good lives

verse.speaker: Yajnavalkya
verse.setting: Yajnavalkya on how a person becomes what they are.
verse.sanskrit: अथो खल्वाहुः काममय एवायं पुरुष इति स यथाकामो भवति तत्क्रतुर्भवति यत्क्रतुर्भवति तत्कर्म कुरुते यत्कर्म कुरुते तदभिसम्पद्यते ॥
verse.line: As your desire, so your will; as your will, so your deeds; as your deeds, so you become.
verse.translation: And so they say: a person is made of desire. As his desire is, so is his will; as his will is, so is his deed; and whatever deed he does, that he becomes.
verse.why: You become what you desire and do; know what matters while you are here.

prasang.title: Yajnavalkya on desire and death
prasang.summary: Yajnavalkya explains what happens at death with images of a caterpillar and a goldsmith. A person becomes what they desire, will and do; one who knows the self has nothing left to fret about. Know it while you are here, he says, don't brood over many words, and live calm and collected.
prasang.lesson: You become what you desire and do; know what matters while you are here.

verse.for_you: Bhartrihari spoke of a life that lasts only a few blinks. Today, Yajnavalkya shows how desire becomes your will and your deeds. You are not fixed yet; you are still becoming.
verse.try_today: Notice one small thing you do today because you want to.

why: As your desire, so you become (Brihadaranyaka Upanishad 4.4.5)
shows where a want leads, step by step, before it has become a life

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the power of understanding to end confusion and guilt.
verse.sanskrit: योगसंन्यस्तकर्माणं ज्ञानसंछिन्नसंशयम् । आत्मवन्तं न कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय ॥
verse.line: Doubts cut away by understanding, steady within, your actions stop binding you.
verse.translation: Actions do not bind one who has renounced action through yoga, whose doubts are cut away by knowledge, and who is self-possessed, Dhananjaya.
verse.why: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.

prasang.title: The glory of knowledge
prasang.summary: Krishna praises knowledge: learn it humbly from those who know, it carries even the worst wrongdoer across, faith and self-control bring it, and doubt destroys. He ends: cut your doubt and stand up.
prasang.lesson: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.

verse.try_today: Notice one action today done without needing a result.
verse.scene_line: You stand at the edge of knowing and not knowing, while Krishna offers you the stillness of self-possession.

why: Cut the doubt with understanding, then stand up.
doubt is cut by knowledge

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
verse.sanskrit: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कार्याकार्ये भयाभये । बन्धं मोक्षं च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी ॥
verse.line: Clear judgement knows when to act and when to wait, what to fear, and what frees you.
verse.translation: The understanding that knows action and withdrawal, what should and should not be done, what is to be feared and what not, bondage and freedom, that understanding is sattvic, Partha.

words.en: in what should be done and not done

verse.why: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

prasang.title: Knowledge, action, doer, intellect, resolve and happiness by the three gunas
prasang.summary: Krishna describes clear, restless and dull versions of action, doer, judgement, resolve and happiness: the best joy is poison first and nectar later; the restless kind is nectar first and poison later.
prasang.lesson: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

verse.try_today: Notice one choice today where waiting is wiser than acting.

why: Telling the good from the pleasant is the text's own opposite of confusion.
describes the clear judgement that can tell when to act and when to step back

verse.speaker: Shiva
verse.setting: Shiva, met on the road by the doubt-ridden Garuda, sends him to good company instead of answering.
verse.sanskrit: मिलेहु गरुड़ मारग महँ मोही। कवन भाँति समुझावौं तोही॥ तबहिं होइ सब संसय भंगा। जब बहु काल करिअ सतसंगा ॥
verse.line: Doubts don't end in a passing conversation. They clear with long time in good company.
verse.translation: You met me on the road; how can I explain it to you in passing? All doubts end only when one spends a long time in good company.
verse.why: Doubt is human; stay long enough in good company and it can lead somewhere better.

prasang.title: Garuda's doubt
prasang.summary: Garuda, Vishnu's own mount, frees Ram from a serpent-noose in battle and starts to doubt: how can God be bound? He goes to Narada, Brahma and Shiva, who sends him to an old crow, Kakbhushundi, saying doubts clear only with long time in good company. Kakbhushundi tells him no one has escaped delusion, desire, craving or anger; Garuda ends up grateful for the doubt that led him there.
prasang.story_hook: The great eagle Garuda flew to a crow to ask a question.
prasang.lesson: Doubt is human; stay long enough in good company and it can lead somewhere better.

verse.for_you: Yesterday you heard about clear judgment. Today you can trust that staying near what you love will show you what is real. Good company does not rush you. It simply stays with you until the fog lifts.
verse.try_today: Sit near someone you trust and say nothing.

why: trust grows by staying near those who have it

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Ashma (quoted by Vyasa)
verse.setting: The sage Ashma answers King Janaka, who asks how to bear the loss of family and wealth.
verse.sanskrit: क्वासे क्व च गमिष्यामि कोऽन्वहं किमिहास्थितः / कस्मात्किमनुशोचेयमित्येवं स्थापयेन्मनः
verse.line: In grief, ask: where did I come from, where am I going, who am I? Let that steady you.
verse.translation: 'Where was I before? Where will I go? Who am I, really, and why am I here? Why should I grieve, and for what?' Ask these, and steady the mind.
verse.why: Days don't come back. Grieve, then steady yourself with the people still in front of you.
verse.misuse: These questions are for steadying grief, not for dismissing it; mourning is natural.

prasang.title: Ashma Gita: the sage on bearing loss
prasang.summary: Vyasa tells the grieving Yudhishthira how the sage Ashma consoled King Janaka: pain comes from what we didn't want or what we lost; meetings end; days don't return; ask who you are and steady the mind.
prasang.lesson: Days don't come back. Grieve, then steady yourself with the people still in front of you.

verse.for_you: Yesterday, good company stayed with you. Today, steady the mind by asking where you were, where you go, and who you are.
verse.try_today: Ask yourself where you were before, where you are going, and who you are.

why: Meeting and parting come to all; the mind's pain is met with understanding.
Self-inquiry as a steadying practice
